kevin: heads up — gpu-23 (us-west) started spitting Xid 31s around 03:12 UTC yesterday, intermittent reboots. dmesg/journal is noisy, attaching snippets below. can infra help speed triage?

kevin: ```[  100.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=1234, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  100.123789] kernel: nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus
[  100.124000] nvidia-smi: GPU 0: Unreachable or ECC errors
```

maria: ugh, ok. first steps: capture kernel ring + journal for the boot where it happened, and nv-smi snapshot. run on the node:```sudo journalctl -k -b -1 > /tmp/node-kernel-lastboot.txt; sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -b -1 > /tmp/nvidia-persistenced.txt; nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR > /tmp/nvidia-errors.txt```then tar up and drop in our s3 bucket. also include /var/log/messages or /var/log/syslog depending on distro. :point_up:```

jia: also useful: quick grep for Xid/ECC timestamps and a small context window. i use:```sudo journalctl -k -b -1 --no-pager | grep -E -n "Xid|ECC|GPU has fallen off" -n | sed -n '1,200p'```then timestamp-align to `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,POWER -lms 1000` samples if it's flaky. :eyes:```

oliver: small heuristics we've used before: correlate Xid 31 with either PCI bus resets, ECC corrected/uncc errors, or power cycling. check ECC counters:```nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.errors.corrected, memory.errors.uncorrected --format=csv,noheader,nounits```if uncorrected >0 it's usually a hardware tilt and we should DRain+replace asap. if corrected spikes then watch but defer replacement. also check BIOS firmware + driver revision mismatch — paste `modinfo nvidia | grep version` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,firmware_version --format=csv`.

sre-bot: node-status gpu-23: cordon=false, drained=false, last-reboot=2025-11-09T03:15:12Z, pending-alarms=GPU_XID_31 (1). Suggested action: collect bundle -> triage -> cordon if repeat >2 in 24h.

tim: oncall here. if you can capture an immediate bundle run this one-liner and upload to slack thread:```sudo mkdir -p /tmp/gpu-triage && sudo journalctl -k -b -1 > /tmp/gpu-triage/journal-kernel.txt && sudo dmesg -T > /tmp/gpu-triage/dmesg.txt && nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/gpu-triage/nvidia-smi.txt && sudo tar czf /tmp/gpu-23-bundle-$(date +%s).tgz -C /tmp/gpu-triage . && sha256sum /tmp/gpu-23-bundle-*.tgz```That gives us everything for correlation. If you see more Xids within an hour, cordon the node and file a hardware ticket (cc hwops).```

maria: for parsing at scale we run a small python/grep pipeline that extracts candidate windows (±5s) around Xid events and collapses repeated identical stack traces. saves 80% time vs reading raw logs. gist (very short):```python -c "import sys,re;d=sys.stdin.read();print('\n'.join({m.group(0) for m in re.finditer('.{0,120}Xid.{0,120}',d)}))" < journal-kernel.txt```we can drop a sanitized helper in infra repo if helpful.

kevin: running the bundle now, uploading to S3 and will paste link. thanks — will run ECC counters and driver info too. if it repeats i'll cordon per runbook. :thumbsup:

kevin: uploaded: https://s3.company/internal-triage/gpu-23-bundle-1745004321.tgz (perm: infra-triage)

oliver: got the bundle, starting quick grep. initial look: driver_version 560.45, firmware 12.3.0, corrected errors spiked before Xid, but also a sudden PCI link reset. scheduling node repro window to collect continuous `nvidia-smi -lms 500` for 30m.

maria: if the continuous trace shows power/clock thrashing that's usually PSU or riser. if it's only 1 GPU on the board consider swapping slot before full replacement. record which slot and serial for hw ticket.

tim: good. remind hwops to pull serial if we escalate. set node to cordon if >2 Xid 31 in 24h. I'll annotate the incident ticket.```
